checks.explanation: Vanishing radial inputs do not force a biased distance-value filter to vanish. Its nonzero vector coefficient can reach the cutoff unchanged, then disappear when the edge is removed. This concerns continuity of the mathematical architecture, not rotational equivariance.
checks.demonstration: As \(d\uparrow d_{\mathrm{cut}}\), the radial features tend to zero, but \(D^V=\sigma(W_D^Ve_{\mathrm{RBF}}+b_D^V)\) tends to \(\sigma(b_D^V)\), which may be nonzero. Choose a nonzero allowed value bias and constant scalar value features so that one first-layer directional coefficient tends to \(c\ne0\), with incoming vector features zero. The two-atom vector messages then approach \(\pm c\widehat r\) below the cutoff and become zero above it. To make the jump reach a scalar update without assuming a bias in the output map, add a third atom at a fixed interior distance on the opposite side of the central atom. In the first layer, an affine distance filter can vanish at this fixed edge while remaining nonzero at the cutoff: for a radial feature with value \(r_0>0\) on that edge, choose its preactivation \(1-r/r_0\). Set scalar attention to zero in this layer. In the second layer, choose a nonzero scalar-attention contribution from the fixed interior edge and map it to \(q^2=1\), while setting the other scalar coefficients to zero. The cutoff edge contributes vanishing scalar attention. With \(U_1=U_2=I\), Equation (10) then contributes \(c^2\) below the cutoff and zero above it in the limit. A scalar readout sensitive to that coordinate produces a jump. All choices use the stated filters and coupling and preserve equivariance.
checks.repair: Multiply the entire edgewise vector contribution by a cutoff that vanishes at the boundary, including both \(s^1_{ij}v_j\) and the directional term. With bounded features and continuous downstream operations, the edge contribution then tends to zero and edge deletion is continuous. A cutoff with vanishing first derivative, together with continuously differentiable remaining operations near that configuration, also matches the first derivative across deletion. The official implementation explicitly diagnoses the original architecture’s discontinuity and adds the optional vector_cutoff branch, which tapers the shared scalar/vector value features before splitting them.
checks.scope: The original printed continuity guarantee is not automatic with the allowed distance-filter bias. The implementation supplies an optional correction; this does not establish that every released model enabled it. Rotation equivariance is unaffected.

checks.explanation: Read the complete 76,708-character text (main body, Appendices A-F, references) in gapless ranges. The loss therefore recovers the cluster support and the one-patch collapse is the worst configuration, not the best. The residual limitation is a positive loss floor because the map cannot encode cluster size, i.e. clusters are matched only softly - a design choice, not a false step. Also verified: softmax-over-slots followed by token-axis normalisation is exactly the cited slot-attention scheme (all slot columns sum to 1 in a toy matrix); Eq. (4) is dimensionally consistent with W_up of shape d x D and is an exact identity at initialisation; Eq. (6) is correctly bounded in [0,1] and Appendix C.3's 'substitute 1 for an absent concept' is the multiplicative identity. Reconstructed the finite-state reward as deterministic equality after tool execution; this is a chosen evaluation criterion, not a guarantee of policy-correct interaction. Weighted edit recurrence has nonnegative symmetric tier costs; k-medoids is a heuristic with a finite iteration cap, not a claimed globally optimal clustering solver.
